findings.passage: The Daily Beast headlined its response "Why Is Chris Pratt Lying About His Religious Past?" The same piece named other causes for the hostility.
findings.problem: This misattributes quotations, and the edit introduced it (the draft ended at the headline). "The same piece" follows the Daily Beast headline, so readers will take Gunn's "literally just made up... about his politics" and "the writer noted that 'none of this noise has hurt his box-office prowess or his reputation in town'" as the Daily Beast's. I opened the full Daily Beast article (Kyndall Cunningham, June 30, 2022) via a Wayback raw copy, and it contains neither line. Both are from the Men's Health profile: Gunn quoted by Mickey Rapkin, and Rapkin's own aside. The Daily Beast argues the opposite, calling the 'not a religious person' line "absolute bullshit". The passage credits a reassuring defense to his harshest critic in a sensitive-allegation section. The attribution sentence is not in the evidence inventory; c-other-causes correctly cites only src-mh-2022.
findings.acceptance_test: The prose names Men's Health (optionally its writer, Mickey Rapkin) as the source of both the Gunn quote and the box-office aside. No sentence attributes them to The Daily Beast. The Daily Beast is described only by what its article says (its headline, and if wanted its argument that the remark contradicts his public record). The repaired attribution sentence falls inside c-other-causes' passage or a new claim citing src-mh-2022.

findings.passage: He didn't mention _Mercy_, his January thriller, which drew 24 percent positive reviews
findings.problem: This is false, and the edit introduced it. In the same Not Dead Yet answer (about 48:15-48:30), all three transcriptions (research small.en, edit large-v3-turbo, and my independent medium.en) have Pratt say: "I've been playing this Terminal List character James Reese and then I've been doing some other things, Mercy I did recently". He named Mercy as a recent role; he did not mention its reception. The src-not-dead-yet-2026 context says only that he "does not mention Mercy's reception", and c-mercy's inference ("while noting he did not cite it") repeats the prose error. The preceding paraphrase, "His recent roles had carried a seriousness, he said", is one-sided. Two of three models hear "there's a certain irreverence in some of the roles that I've done and then there's more of a seriousness in some" (small.en: "a reverence"). The answer was about having played both kinds and wanting more comedy.
findings.acceptance_test: The closing paragraph no longer says he didn't mention Mercy. It either says he listed Mercy among his recent roles without discussing its reception, or it drops any claim about what he omitted. Mercy's reception stays labelled as the author's context. His reasons are reported as he gave them, as a paraphrase, with 'irreverence' quoted only after a human listen. c-mercy's passage and inference are updated, and the corrected assertion cites src-not-dead-yet-2026 with the ~48:20 timestamp.

findings.problem: The cited source, Wikipedia, calls Everwood (2002-2006) his first regular television role and starring role, and calls Andy Dwyer on Parks and Recreation his "breakthrough role". 'Broke through' on Everwood contradicts it.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence calls Everwood his first regular TV role, or similar wording supported by src-wikipedia, and does not call it his breakthrough. c-bio-career's claim and passage match.

findings.passage: In 2022 he said he had never been to Hillsong, the church he had been linked to, and attends Zoe Church, though not exclusively.
findings.problem: His denial is attributed correctly, but the article gives no relevant response, as the standard requires for disputed claims. The full Daily Beast piece (June 30, 2022), already a source here, says he "had also been previously photographed attending a service at Hillsong's L.A. branch back in 2017". It also reports that Zoe's pastor told The New York Times he modeled Zoe on Hillsong. The research stage could read only the opening. c-hillsong-never's alternative and src-daily-beast-2022's locator and excerpt don't reflect the full text.
findings.acceptance_test: Option one: the paragraph adds, attributed to The Daily Beast (2022), its report that he had been photographed at a Hillsong Los Angeles service in 2017, without endorsing it. Option two: the resolution records a concrete reason for leaving it out. Either way, c-hillsong-never's alternative records the counter-report and src-daily-beast-2022's locator and excerpt reflect the full article.

findings.problem: The body is 4,336 words, about 800 over the standard's ~2,000-3,500 target and near the 4,500 ceiling. findings.acceptance_test: The body is cut to about 3,500-3,900 words. Cuts must not remove protected passages, the Seven/Nine/Six tests, the restored GQ context or any repair.
